I do love Cockroach, but the old licensing model was pretty brutal if you required any enterprise features (ex: incremental backup).
For me it was the multiple regions. It's like.. with that disabled why are we even here? Data residency is the whole point...
The only thing I don't like is the mandatory telemetry.
I don't like the fact that even free users need an annual license key.
Spanner is cheap in comparison depending on your storage requirements. I've seen CockroachDB quoted as 10x more, and for a product that is harder to sell to stake holders.
Cockroach is basically Spanner usable outside of Google. So global transaction with cluster world wide.
Not all alternatives listed are ACID compliant with serializable transactions like CockroachDB is.

I love cockroachdb to death, but the key features that prevent me from using it in any real projects I'm doing are the backup/restore feature, which is currently locked behind their enterprise version. I also would love to use CDC and table partitioning.
I stopped using them when they released Follower-Reads as an enterprise feature. I'm back to Postgres for now.
